title: Practise a food recall: find every affected shipment
summary: A small food producer may know ingredient lots but struggle to show which dispatched packs contain one selected lot.
audience: Small batch food producers using CSV exports or spreadsheets.
why_it_matters: A drill exposes missing links before someone needs to make a real hold decision. Current evidence is mostly vendor testimony.
proposed_fix: Import ingredient receipts, production lots and dispatches. Trace a selected lot, reconcile quantities, and require the operator to resolve gaps before exporting a drill record.
example: A jam maker selects a sample sugar lot, finds two affected batches, and records which sample customer shipments would be held.
flow: Import and map three CSV files.
Select a lot and resolve broken links.
Confirm a simulated hold list and export the drill.
deliverable: A usable local drill tool producing a customer shipment list, quantity reconciliation and unresolved-evidence register.
question: Can a producer finish a traceability drill faster without silently missing an affected dispatch?
measure: Affected-shipment recall, false inclusions, unexplained quantity and minutes to a signed drill.
baseline: Manual joins and filtering in a spreadsheet.
alternative: ReciPal already traces inventory and customer records. Other vendor comparisons describe recall tools; their detailed claims remain unverified.
proposed_difference: A portable drill across existing exports, with explicit missing-link blocks. This gap has not been validated against existing products.
risk: Incorrect units, rework and mixed batches can break tracing. This slice excludes live recalls and does not certify legal compliance.
data_plan: Development fixtures: Self-authored CSV fixtures under CC0, under 1MB. Include split lots, waste and a deliberately missing dispatch link. No real business records. The finished tool must also accept the user's own manually supplied inputs in its supported format; sample-only output is not completion.
model_plan: No model. Deterministic graph traversal and quantity checks.
why_ml: ML is unnecessary for traceability. It would obscure exact links.
venture: Possible fixed subscription for repeated drills and saved mappings. No billing or paid integration in the slice.
market: Small spreadsheet-based producers are a proposed segment. Market size and willingness to pay are unverified.
customer_test: Later, with owner-arranged testers, compare the same drill in their existing tool. No outreach performed.
week_test: Acceptance: import six sample lots, select the contaminated sample input, identify all four affected dispatches, repair one missing link, and export an operator-confirmed hold list. Block export as complete while the link is unresolved.
effort: 5–7 focused development days for CSV import, tracing, corrections and export.
feasibility: Good for a local laptop or 4GB VPS at a few thousand rows. No OCR, ERP integrations or live messaging.
next: Build the six-lot fixture and manually verify its expected affected shipments before implementing.
reason: Current operational account and explicit missing drill feature support a concrete test, although competitors weaken the commercial case.
evidence: S09 current maker account; S10 current competing capability; S11 current vendor-authored corroboration. No independent buyer validation.
evidence_level: Current vendor evidence; exploratory product gap.

title: Turn a scrambled PDF into a readable, keyboard-friendly copy
summary: A reader can extract text from a PDF yet encounter columns and headings in the wrong order.
audience: Blind readers and people preparing short accessible documents.
why_it_matters: Reading order determines whether the user can follow instructions. A current blind developer reports this problem while building a competing reader.
proposed_fix: For short text-bearing PDFs, expose extracted blocks in a keyboard editor. Let the user reorder, label headings and inspect source anchors, then export a navigable HTML reading copy.
example: A volunteer fixes a two-column event guide so a screen-reader user reaches the venue instructions in the intended order.
flow: Open a short text-bearing PDF.
Reorder blocks and mark headings by keyboard.
Navigate and save the corrected HTML copy.
deliverable: A reusable accessible reading copy with headings, source-page links and an explicit list of omitted or unsupported content.
question: Does explicit correction help users finish a reading task more reliably than extraction alone?
measure: Task completion, order errors, omitted blocks and keyboard actions.
baseline: Plain text extraction with source-page links.
alternative: Lumen Vision is already developing a reader; Outloud already checks accessibility. Acrobat and platform readers are established alternatives, but detailed current remediation parity was not verified.
proposed_difference: A small, editable reading-copy workflow with transparent source anchors. It must prove an advantage over those readers.
risk: Tables, maths and scans exceed the week scope. HTML export is not certified PDF remediation. Accessibility must be tested with actual assistive technology.
data_plan: Development fixtures: Self-authored PDFs with known order and licence CC0. At most 20 pages per file and 10MB; no private uploads or downloaded document corpus. The finished tool must also accept the user's own manually supplied inputs in its supported format; sample-only output is not completion.
model_plan: Week one uses text geometry and user correction. A compact ranker is optional future work, not a prerequisite.
why_ml: Not needed to ship the first useful correction loop. A model only earns inclusion by reducing correction work without omissions.
venture: Potential subscription for frequent reading-copy preparation. Recurring willingness to pay is unknown.
market: Accessibility need is observed; the proposed purchasing segment is unvalidated.
customer_test: Later compare one real reading task with an owner-arranged assistive-technology user. No recruitment now.
week_test: Acceptance: a keyboard-only operator repairs a two-column three-page fixture, saves HTML, reopens it, reaches each heading in correct order, and follows a source-page link. All original text blocks remain accounted for.
effort: 5–7 days with strict text-bearing PDF scope.
feasibility: Local browser/server and bounded files fit laptop/4GB targets. No OCR or large vision model.
next: Define keyboard interactions and create a fixture with an explicit gold reading order.
reason: Concrete accessibility task with current first-person evidence, tempered by an active competing product.

evidence_level: Current first-person maker evidence; usability and competitive gap unverified.

Review dates, redact details and state the request.

Review comparable failures and evidence gaps.
Choose the next experiment and export the packet.

title: Which scrambled document sections should a reviewer fix first?
summary: A document parser can produce plausible text with an order mistake that makes instructions unusable.
audience: Accessible-document reviewers and applied document-AI researchers.
why_it_matters: Current RPD research improves structured document understanding, but large-model accuracy does not directly measure useful correction order on a small computer.
proposed_fix: Study a small learned ranker of suspicious block pairs. Evaluate whether it prioritises harmful order errors under a fixed review budget.
example: A reviewer has time to inspect ten block pairs; the ranking should expose a reversed instruction sequence before a harmless footer difference.
flow: Create gold block orders and controlled errors.
Compare rules and learned rankings on held-out templates.
Measure corrected order errors per review budget.
deliverable: Research report, reproducible small benchmark and a calibrated error-ranking experiment; not a full PDF remediation product.
question: Does a compact learned ranking improve correction yield over geometry rules without missing critical order breaks?
measure: Pairwise order errors found at budgets 5/10/20, missed critical breaks, CPU latency and peak RAM. Human benefit remains unproven without a later approved user study.
baseline: Geometry and heading rules; Outloud is a closest existing checker, but does not define this ranking experiment.
alternative: RPD/SARA learns document structure with a larger vision-language model. A parser-confidence ranking is a second practical comparator. Compare both conceptually and run only feasible released implementations.

risk: Handmade errors may be unrealistic. Template leakage and disagreement over legitimate reading order can dominate results.

flow: Separate speakers and microphones in the evaluation.
Compare confidence thresholds and calibrated acceptance.
Measure wrong acceptances against confirmation burden.

title: Will missing sensor readings point to the wrong past breakdown?
summary: An operator may retrieve the wrong historical incident when missing sensor readings are filled with plausible but wrong values.
why_it_matters: ExactCert gives distance guarantees only inside supplied value bounds. TSGuard shows that constrained imputation and operational fallback are already active research.
proposed_fix: Study how calibrated bounds and missingness patterns change nearest-incident decisions. Separate mathematical certification inside a box from the chance that the true signal lies outside it.
example: A temperature window is missing during an event; the system returns 'ambiguous' when two historical cases cannot be reliably ordered.
flow: Mask known signal windows and preserve the hidden truth.
Compare imputation and interval-based retrieval.
Measure incorrect confident retrieval and abstention.
deliverable: A reproducible decision-level comparison, interval calibration analysis and failure cases.
question: Can calibrated intervals reduce wrong accepted neighbours under drift without making nearly every query ambiguous?
measure: Wrong accepted top-1 matches, accepted coverage, true-value interval coverage, interval width, latency and RAM.
baseline: Linear interpolation and last observation carried forward, followed by L1 nearest-neighbour retrieval.
alternative: ExactCert supplies interval distance bounds; TSGuard supplies constrained learned point estimates. Compare their assumptions and operational decisions, not just imputation RMSE.
proposed_difference: Stress-test bound miscoverage under drift and measure downstream retrieval errors. ExactCert already compares several imputers, so another imputation accuracy table is insufficient.
risk: Synthetic drift may favour the proposed bounds. A certificate is invalid as a truth guarantee when values leave the assumed box.
data_plan: Generate CC0 thermal-process sequences with known missing truth for pilot. UCI Air Quality has conflicting research-only body and CC BY footer; hold acquisition until terms are resolved. No private plant data.
model_plan: Small quantile regression for bounds plus ExactCert-style separable L1 bounds. Compare to empirical bounds and point imputation. Full TSGuard replication depends on code/licence/compute checks.
why_ml: Learned conditional bounds may adapt to operating regime, but must beat simple fixed empirical intervals.
venture: Possible future retrieval guard; no industrial product validation.
market: Research relevance only. No plant buyer or incident cost estimate established.
customer_test: Offline blinded retrieval against known full windows; later operator interpretation would need separately arranged access.
week_test: CPU pilot: 2,000 synthetic windows of length 32, 200 held-out queries, time-ordered split and two drift settings. Compare at matched coverage under 3GB. Not run.
effort: One week for synthetic decision experiment; masters-scale work adds licensed real signals and drift analysis.
feasibility: Good small CPU pilot. Real-data conclusions remain conditional. Use separable L1, not the paper's expensive general dynamic programme.
next: Implement a truth-known fixture and verify the simple bound arithmetic against exhaustive tiny cases.
reason: Current explicit guarantee assumptions create a testable question with a practical decision.
evidence: ExactCert October 29 and TSGuard October 2 are current primary methods; neither establishes customer demand.
evidence_level: Current research; real-data terms unresolved.
originality: Bound validity and decision evaluation under shift; no claimed new certification theorem.
buyer: None required; future maintenance team is hypothetical.
growth_path: Add real operating regimes after data terms and retrieval labels are established.
contribution: Separate interval miscoverage from retrieval uncertainty and quantify their costs.
cpu_pilot: 2,000 short synthetic windows; linear/quantile models; exact L1 bounds.
ltu_fit: Applied industrial AI with measurable uncertainty; no supervisor or company access assumed.
